A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoLLaVA-8K and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A.1–A.8. Relocated figures and renumbered appendix tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original XLRS-Bench evaluations, token-ablation experiments, and training-data and compression ablations, including Appendix A.4.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds efficiency measurements, component ablations, small-object evaluations, and LRS-VQA results in Tables 5–8.

M1.justification: The LESS-based data selection, Background Token Pruning, Anchored Token Selection, and LLaVA-based training and inference procedures are retained. The new component ablations test variants without revising the proposed final method.

E1.justification: V2 evaluates LRS-VQA, which v1 only discussed as prior work, extending evaluation within remote-sensing VQA. It also evaluates a small-object-focused XLRS-Bench subset. The training datasets, sensor domain, and overall task scope remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 Table 6 introduces data-only and BTP-without-ATS comparison conditions, with the latter reporting OOM, beyond v1's dataset-source and compression-ratio comparisons. The external-model rosters in the retained benchmark tables are unchanged; the new benchmark and subset evaluations reuse LLaVA-Next.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds several evaluation protocols: converting LRS-VQA to four-option questions using generated distractors and structural validation; selecting 1,570 small-object samples using image-area thresholds; and measuring FLOPs and latency across compression settings, including new 48× and 96× settings. The original training configuration and XLRS-Bench protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained appendix ablations, v2 adds a data-versus-token-optimization ablation, expands compression sensitivity analysis with computational measurements, and evaluates preservation of small-object information. These address additional questions about component contributions, efficiency tradeoffs, and object-scale robustness.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, training seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the evaluated results. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and appendix scores remain unchanged, including the 51.5% main average. Added results include small-object overall scores of 40.3% versus 34.1% for LLaVA-Next, and LRS-VQA accuracy of 56.28% versus 55.07%. Table 5 adds efficiency results: 24× versus 96× compression yields 198.06 versus 51.13 TFLOPs, 2.17 versus 1.46 seconds/image, and 51.5% versus 49.7% accuracy. These are additional comparisons, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: The influence-score formulation, clustering constraint, attention equation, and autoregressive formulation are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are substantively added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: two high-resolution training datasets, two token-management strategies, 8K-capable GeoLLaVA, and leading XLRS-Bench performance. The added analyses support these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning computational scalability, small-object preservation, and external generalization, plus a limitation that CLS attention can favor one dominant region. It also attributes most gains to token optimization, although Table 6 reports a larger increment from data alone: 44.7 to 49.1, followed by 51.5 with token optimization. Existing appendix limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code/data availability from a planned release to a reported completed release at the same project link. Appendix A.7 still describes future distribution, so actual availability is not consistently established by the PDFs. V2 also documents distractor generation and validation for the new LRS-VQA evaluation; existing implementation and training details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 removes the related-work description of LRS-VQA's 7,333 questions, eight categories, and maximum image length, and instead discusses it as an external generalization benchmark. The same cited work remains, renumbered from reference 21 to 59. Both versions cite the same 61 works, with no broader novelty or literature-positioning revision.

P1.justification: Section 5 gains Main Results and Further Analyses subsections with localized explanatory additions. Affiliations are adjusted and acknowledgements added. Most existing prose, section order, and appendix organization are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 adds four analytical tables and substantially rearranges main-text displays. Figures 4 and 6 become smaller figures with surrounding text, other displays are repositioned, and Table 4 precedes its results discussion. Existing figure content is retained, while appendix Tables 5–9 become Tables 9–13.

improvement.justification: The new efficiency measurements, component comparisons, and small-object and external evaluations usefully strengthen evidence beyond v1's existing analyses. The benefit is limited by sparse details for the new protocols and overinterpretation: Table 6's reported increments of 4.4 points from data and 2.4 from token optimization contradict the claim that token optimization supplies most gains. Overall, the added evidence provides a modest quality improvement.
